entries.cost_expression: When thinking, rehearsal, or option management continues to be prolonged, real entry and commitment may be delayed; this prompts the need to set stopping conditions and reality check points.
entries.description: It is easier to process reality starting from understanding, anticipation, possibility, security and space for choice.
entries.observation_question: Is your judgment today helping you take action, or is it delaying your entry into real-life interactions?
entries.strength_expression: In scenarios where information, risks, and paths need to be sorted out, this set of clues may help you discover structures and information gaps.
entries.stress_signal: Start over-rehearsing, keep options open, delay entering the market, or replace experience with ideas.

entries.boundary_note: Stance is a theoretical grouping, not a behavioral style measure, extraversion judgment, leadership rating, or stable personality classification.
entries.cost_expression: If pushing becomes a habitual response, fatigue, limitations, loss, or relationship costs may be seen later; review should return to the specific event rather than treating it as a fixed flaw.
entries.description: In the Enneagram stance theory, the assertive group is often used to describe a tendency to push outward faster, occupy space, or pull the rhythm. It can only be used as a situational observation clue and cannot indicate that you are active, strong or outgoing in all situations.
entries.observation_question: When you take the initiative today, are you actually protecting goals, relationships, boundaries, or feelings of uncertainty? Is there a scene where you were able to stop and pace yourself as well?
entries.strength_expression: When the goal is clear, the situation is stagnant, or someone needs to take the lead, this set of clues may help you drive the pace, bear the cost of advancement, and push the next step forward; you still need to check other people's resources and true authorization.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include faster tempo, increased intensity, harder pauses, or putting aside vulnerabilities and limitations.

entries.boundary_note: Stance is a theoretical grouping, not a compliance measure, moral evaluation, relationship diagnosis, or stable personality classification.
entries.cost_expression: If the sense of responsibility becomes a habitual reaction, "I agree" and "I should" may be mixed up, and the true needs will be expressed later; this requires calibrating the responsibility boundary with specific events.
entries.description: In Enneagram stance, the compliant group is often used to describe a tendency to act with reference to responsibilities, rules, relationship obligations, or trustworthy standards. It can only be used as a situational observation clue, but it does not mean that you are always submissive, ingratiating, or lacking in assertiveness.
entries.observation_question: When you take on something today, does it actually come from recognition, relationship responsibility, risk prediction, or fear of disappointing people? Is there a scenario where you could also clearly say no or renegotiate?
entries.strength_expression: When a promise needs to be fulfilled, a rule needs to be seen, or a relationship needs someone to take responsibility for, this set of clues may help you put responsibility into specific actions.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include taking too much responsibility, double-checking, taking too much care of others, or having a hard time shutting down your inner “shoulds.”

entries.boundary_note: Stance is a theoretical grouping, not a measure of avoidance, an assessment of sociability, a clinical judgment, or a stable personality classification.
entries.cost_expression: If holding space becomes a habitual reaction, the action of returning to the scene may become delayed, and observation, numbness, or self-world may temporarily replace real action; this needs to be checked with specific situations.
entries.description: In Enneagram theory, the withdrawn group is often used to describe a tendency to turn inward to organize feelings, energy, understanding, or rhythm before deciding when to enter the scene. It can only be used as a situational observation clue, but it cannot mean that you are always avoiding, being cold, or lacking in action.
entries.observation_question: When you step back today, are you actually restoring energy, organizing information, protecting relationships, or avoiding conflict? Is there a scene where you were able to re-enter and take a stand as well?
entries.strength_expression: When information is overloaded, emotions need to be settled, or the pace of the scene is too fast, this set of clues may help you retain space and organize internal clues; if there is a lack of action to return to the scene, it may also be misinterpreted as exiting.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include being quieter, more withdrawn, more procrastinating, or having difficulty bringing stance and needs back to real interactions.

entries.boundary_note: Harmonics are stress coping cues, not emotion regulation ability scores, mental health judgments, moral evaluations, or stable personality classifications.
entries.cost_expression: If de-escalation becomes an inertial response, problems may be dismissed prematurely and real losses, boundaries or conflict issues postponed; this requires going back to the specific incident for verification.
entries.description: In the Enneagram harmonic theory, the positive outlook group is often used to observe whether people tend to ease the situation, reconstruct meaning, lighten the atmosphere, or find an exit when faced with disappointment, friction, or pressure. It is not a measure of optimism, nor does it indicate that you avoid problems.
entries.observation_question: When you say "nothing" or try to lighten the mood today, are you actually restoring flexibility, protecting relationships, or letting important issues go out of sight for the time being?
entries.strength_expression: When you are under short-term pressure, the team atmosphere is sinking, or the relationship needs to be stabilized first, this set of clues may help you retain hope, reduce the sense of collapse, and gain space for subsequent processing; it is not proof of avoiding the problem.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include rushing to turn the page, convincing yourself that it’s okay, or hiding the real costs with kindness, optimism, changing the subject, and following along.

entries.boundary_note: Harmonic is a stress response cue, not an evaluation of ability, a rating of rationality, a judgment of emotional maturity, or a classification of stable personality.
entries.cost_expression: If dealing with problems becomes a habitual reaction, emotional and relationship costs may be skipped, and human problems may be prematurely technicalized; when reviewing, you need to look at who was affected at the time.
entries.description: In the Enneagram harmonic theory, the competency group is often used to observe whether people tend to use standards, efficiency, structures, or executable steps to bring the situation back to order when faced with problems, pressure, or a sense of loss of control. It is not a measure of ability, nor does it indicate that you are always rational or apathetic.
entries.observation_question: When you turn problems into tasks today, are you actually restoring order and preventing loss of control, or are you avoiding the cost that people and relationships are suffering?
entries.strength_expression: When there is confusion, information is scattered, or responsibilities need to be implemented, this set of clues may help you organize the problem, break it down into tasks, and make the next step executable; the conclusion still needs to be tested by the situation and feedback from others.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include cold expressions, increased speed, an overemphasis on the right thing to do, or acting like you are fixing the system rather than confronting the person who is being affected.

entries.boundary_note: Harmonic is a stress coping cue, not a mood stability diagnosis, impulsivity measure, relationship risk label, or stable personality classification.
entries.cost_expression: If a strong reaction becomes a habitual reaction, the power of expression may be seen first, but the real need, worry or injury point is covered up; this requires going back to the trigger point for review.
entries.description: In the Enneagram harmonic theory, the reactive group is often used to observe whether people tend to express tension first in situations that are unreal, unstable, unfair, or threatening. It’s not an emotional label, nor does it mean you’re always impulsive or difficult.
entries.observation_question: What is your strong reaction actually protecting today: truth, fairness, safety, boundaries, or some more sensitive point of hurt?
entries.strength_expression: When issues are suppressed, risks are downplayed, or boundaries are violated, this set of cues may help you let the cracks surface and resist pretending that nothing is wrong; the intensity of expression still needs to serve fact-checking and repair.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include being quicker to react, quicker to defend or test others, and more difficult to distinguish between expressing a need or protecting a wound first.

entries.copy: The E105 five-point Likert form uses rating responses to form a full nine-type profile, top three candidates, a leading-candidate gap, and close-call comparison within one scoring context. It is a starting point for self-observation, and its scores are interpreted only within E105.

The FC144 two-option forced-choice form records relative preference signals across paired choices and can provide another observation after a close-call result. Both forms have the same evidence status. FC144 does not replace E105's primary candidate, top three candidates, or raw scoring facts, and its results are interpreted only within the FC144 scoring context.

E105 and FC144 use the same Enneagram interpretation framework but different response tasks, scoring sources, and error structures, so they do not share a scoring space. History, sharing, PDF, and retest surfaces retain each form's source. The page does not directly compare their values or interpret cross-form differences in the top three candidates as personality change.

Cross-form comparison is disabled. Unless a validated equivalence mapping becomes available, E105 and FC144 remain in separate scoring contexts, and history, sharing, and result-review surfaces do not infer improvement, decline, health status, or measurement precision from their differences.

This result supports personality-pattern reflection, self-observation, and dialogue. Current research does not support treating the Enneagram as a well-validated clinical scale. It is not used for mental-health judgment, treatment recommendations, hiring, job matching, competency evaluation, or individual risk assessment. Scores, leading candidates, close-call, diffuse, and response-quality states remain hypotheses to check against real situations.

A user-confirmed type records the user's own resonance after observation. It is not a system rescore or external confirmation. History and sharing surfaces present it only as a self-observation note; it does not overwrite the primary candidate, top three candidates, scorer output, or original scoring facts.

When triggered by low-quality signals, the results are still readable, but the interpretation boundaries are significantly narrowed. The page only retains light observation suggestions to avoid extending a single low-stability answer into a deterministic type of judgment; it gives priority to suggestions for retesting the same question type when the state is more stable and time is more sufficient. Switching forms can serve as another observation, but should not be used as a way to circumvent quality boundaries, find better answers, demonstrate personality changes, or compare score gains and losses.

Diffuse means the nine type signals do not yet form a clear leading pattern. The page lowers certainty about any one number and prioritizes the top three candidates, center distribution, recent counterexamples, and a seven-day observation task. Retesting provides another response sample; it does not automatically correct the result to a particular type.

A close-call means the first and second candidates are close. The page turns their differences into side-by-side comparison, counterexample checks, and seven-day observation questions without requiring a forced type decision.

entries.boundary_copy: This step only collects fragments of reality and does not regard single responses as type proof.
entries.example: For example: someone denies the plan in a meeting. Do you want to add facts, prove yourself, and confirm risks first, or do you want to prevent the situation from becoming tense? Remember only one true episode.
entries.prompt: Today, just choose a scene that makes you noticeably tense, want to push forward, want to explain, want to get closer, want to control, or want to move away. Write what happened and what you did first, without rushing to analyze the numbers.
entries.title: Day 1｜Remember only one trigger point

entries.boundary_copy: These are just motivational clues for the day and do not require a final answer to be found in one go.
entries.example: For example: When something is not done as expected, are you uncomfortable more like worrying that it is not right, that you are not seen, that the relationship has become cold, or that your space has been compressed?
entries.prompt: Think back to an uncomfortable moment today: Did you care more about being right, recognized, needed, safe, bounded, free, true expression, or calm? Choose only the closest one and write a sentence of evidence.
entries.title: Day 2｜Look at what you are maintaining

entries.boundary_copy: Day3 feedback will only be entered into the self-observation record and will not rewrite the measurement scores, primary type candidates, or results page explanations.
entries.example: If you are close-calling, treat Top1 and Top2 as two candidate hypotheses and observe them side by side; this feedback only records evidence and does not require forced selection of one of the two.
entries.prompt: No need to stereotype yourself. Just look back at the first three days: Which type of motivation appears slightly more often in the clues? If it's not clear, choose it unclearly and write down a real scene that you can look back on.
entries.title: Day 3｜Light review of the previous three days

entries.boundary_copy: This is a stress script observation only and does not correspond to developmental stage, medical status, or clinical judgment.
entries.example: For example: When things start to get out of control, do you want to straighten the boundaries first, find out more information, or stabilize the situation first?
entries.prompt: Today, observe the first step after stress arises: fight, explain, retreat, please, transfer, control, numb, find someone to confirm, or something else? Only record the first step and how to recover later.
entries.title: Day 4｜Look at the first step under pressure

entries.boundary_copy: What is observed is your interaction needs, not who is right or wrong in the relationship.
entries.example: For example: When the other person’s words make you uncomfortable, what do you want to protect first, your relationship position, dignity, security, boundaries, or your sense of calm?
entries.prompt: Choose a relationship with minor friction and record whether you would rather be understood, recognized, have boundaries respected, promised, needed, or let the situation settle down. Just write about your own needs and behaviors.
entries.title: Day 5｜Needs in relationship friction

entries.boundary_copy: Blind spot only represents low resource usage, does not represent a defect, nor is it a hard judgment by the system.
entries.example: It’s not about whether you can do it, but whether it always appears a step later in a real scene. Just write a sentence of evidence.
entries.prompt: Just look at one less natural resource today: asking for help, saying no, expressing anger, relaxing and enjoying, acknowledging a need, establishing rules, showing initiative, stopping to feel, or taking on conflict.
entries.title: Day 6｜Look at a low-usage resource

entries.boundary_copy: Day7 resonance feedback only records your self-observation evidence and does not trigger a re-judgment by the system, nor will the result be silently rewritten into a new primary type.
entries.example: If it still wobbles, it's not a failure. You can remain unsure, continue reading the Top3, or choose to retest the same question type or FC144 for supplementary observation if needed.
entries.prompt: Look back on the week and don't ask which number was better, just which explanations are more relevant to your daily motivations. You can choose Top1, Top2, Top3, Others or Still Not Sure, and write a sentence of evidence that can be reviewed.
entries.title: Day 7｜Deep Resonance Voting

fallback_template.motivation_difference: Please go back to the core motivation: What do you care more about: standards, relationship position, safety, boundaries, freedom, results, authenticity, or a sense of stability?
fallback_template.observation_question: In the next 7 days, only specific situations, trigger points, first reactions and post-event reviews will be recorded: In key scenes, do you give priority to standards, relationship position, safety, boundaries, freedom, results, sense of reality, or overall stability? Also note counterexamples: scenarios that look like candidates for a certain type, but what really drives you is not its core focus. Close-call is a side-by-side analysis portal. It is not a forced choice, nor can it lead to diagnosis, recruitment screening, ability evaluation or career decision.
fallback_template.pressure_difference: Under pressure, do you more often correct, confirm, disengage, please, toughen, deflect, or calm the situation first?
fallback_template.relationship_difference: In a relationship, how would you rather be treated: to be understood, recognized, needed, to have boundaries respected, to be committed, or to put an end to conflict first?
fallback_template.same_surface: Both may explain some of the similarities in surface style, but the disagreement is usually not about appearance, but about which type of attention is activated first in stressful situations.
fallback_template.work_difference: When advancing tasks, what do you give more priority to: quality, results, risk, space, dominance, or overall stability?

clear_sample.method_boundary: The example only illustrates how a clear results page is organized: how to put together primary candidates, adjacent explanations, and observation reminders. It does not provide scoring reference, personality conclusion, recruitment screening basis, clinical judgment or cross-form numerical comparison, nor can it replace the user's own report payload.
clear_sample.page_1_preview: This reading example identifies No. 8 as the primary candidate, and suggests that No. 3 and No. 1 may also explain part of the results style: focusing on dominance as well as results and quality. Readers should focus on how the page retains the top 3 leads, rather than interpreting the sample numbers as a more mature, healthy, or ideal combination of types.
clear_sample.short_summary: The reading example shows how the results page simultaneously presents Top3, method boundaries, and observable tone when the primary candidate is relatively clear; it is not a norm, a standard answer, or a conclusion template that users should apply.

close_call_sample.method_boundary: The close-call example only shows how uncertainty is converted into pair parsing and observation tasks. The two forms have the same evidence status and separate scoring contexts. The example does not interpret the Top1/Top2 gap as diagnostic evidence or allow sample conclusions to overwrite the top three candidates, resonance, or quality status of the real attempt.
close_call_sample.page_1_preview: This reading sample reads No. 4 and No. 5 side by side: both may be adducted on the surface, but it is necessary to continue to observe which type of clues is more stable in terms of emotional meaning and cognitive space. The focus of the example is how close-call reduces the tone of the assertion, rather than telling the reader that they must choose a certain number when the scores are similar.
close_call_sample.short_summary: The reading example shows how the results page delivers Top1 and Top2 similarities, key differences, and follow-up observation tasks side-by-side during close-call; it is not a forced-choice answer key or a change rule.

diffuse_sample.method_boundary: The diffuse example only illustrates how the diffuse results page should control the intensity of interpretation: Prioritize Structure, Top3, and Observation tasks. It is not intended for use in diagnosis, career decisions, mental health judgments, or quality remediation, nor does it demonstrate that retesting will automatically result in a more realistic phenotype.
diffuse_sample.page_1_preview: A more reliable way to read this sample reading is to read 9, 6, and 2 together and observe how the clues of relationship, security, and tranquility appear together. The examples are deliberately left vague, reminding the reader to examine the situation, response status, and recurring behavioral cues first, rather than rushing to write a number into its final type.
diffuse_sample.short_summary: The reading sample shows how the results page weakens the single-number tone when the distribution is dispersed, and shifts the reading focus back to Top3, three centers, answer quality, and observable tasks; it is not a corrected answer for low-quality answers.

entries.body: Start with the work cues, pace, and collaboration conditions that may draw your attention. Then compare environments that support this pattern with situations that make it costly. These are observation prompts, not conclusions about ability, performance, career fit, or employment decisions.
entries.module_purpose: Put the motivational differences between the primary type and Top3 into real-life task advancement methods, and make it clear that it only provides self-observation and communication clues, and cannot replace skill evidence, work experience, performance data, or organizational situation judgment.
entries.title: Work style summary

entries.body: Focus on the parts where you can contribute more stably to the team, such as closing, advancing, buffering, planning, connecting or structured judgment.
entries.module_purpose: Let users see the real value they bring to collaboration, rather than a general list of advantages.
entries.title: Collaboration advantage

entries.body: Point out the friction you might create in high-pressure or noisy collaborations, and write the costs not as moral criticism but as observable inertia.
entries.module_purpose: Help users see clearly "why others are stuck with me" and provide preventive explanations for relationships and work scenarios.
entries.title: Collaboration friction points

entries.body: Write only P0 Leadership tendencies that can be published online: Are you more likely to lead through standards, results, boundaries, buffers, or support rather than writing a complete management guide.
entries.module_purpose: Provide a shareable "How do you lead people" entry to the results page, leaving structural space for subsequent workplace expansion.
entries.title: leadership model

entries.body: Rather than writing an entire superior-subordinate pairing manual, describe what instructions, cadences, and feedback patterns may make it easier for you to stabilize.
entries.module_purpose: Turn personality reading into a more direct description of the experience of collaboration and being managed.
entries.title: A smoother way to be managed

entries.body: Use specific interaction scenarios to explain how you may express care in a relationship and how you may be misunderstood, and provide counterexamples to avoid inferring relationship needs based on type alone.
entries.module_purpose: Translate personality results into verifiable relationship communication cues: first look at the scenario, behavior and feedback, and then judge whether it fits; not a partner report, nor a conclusion about relationship needs.
entries.title: relationship needs

entries.body: Break the conflict into specific triggers, current misunderstandings, and a utterable repair language to help users review the interaction instead of drawing conclusions about the relationship.
entries.module_purpose: Provide verifiable conflict scripts: identify scenarios and triggers before attempting low-stakes fixes; don’t treat type as an explanation of who is right and who is wrong.
entries.title: conflict script

entries.body: Make communication suggestions into small cards that can be shared: first describe the situation that is easy to be misheard, and then give an expression that can be spoken.
entries.module_purpose: Provide low-certainty communication clues to help users and others calibrate facts, feelings, requests, and boundaries; do not treat types as relationship instructions or fixed rules for getting along.
entries.title: communication instructions

entries.average_expression: In most ordinary situations, people may fall back on familiar strategies for dealing with order, relationships, security, results, or tranquility.
entries.disclaimer: This is a spectrum of self-calibration and interpretation that only describes changes in expression in situations, not medical, mental health, or graded conclusions.
entries.recovery_action: First name the most obvious observable clue at the moment, and then choose a low-risk small action for verification; this is not a treatment suggestion, nor is it used to judge whether the state is good or bad.
entries.stable_expression: When genre inertia is not amplified by high-load situations, genre cues can be used to observe expressions that are more stable and have more leeway.
entries.strained_expression: When task load, interaction tension, or insufficient recovery space are superimposed, the same set of strategies may be used harder and narrower; this is just a review reminder.
